summary: Pre-market: the discount rate sits at the top of its history while risk assets keep advancing, and the repricing is coming from the front end. In the last completed US session the tape was broadly higher, with every tracked mega-cap gaining, led by AMD at 6.359 percent, MU at 5.4989 percent and AVGO at 2.2945 percent, and 20 of 22 tracked sectors and themes finishing positive, led by memory at 4.8923 percent, quantum computing at 4.8867 percent and semis leaders at 4.1739 percent. What is genuinely new overnight is the rate block: the 2-year advanced to 4.74 from 4.67 while the 10-year moved only to 5.01 from 5.00, flattening the 10Y/2Y curve to 0.27 as the 10-year real rate rose to 2.68. The 10-year and the real rate both remain at the 100.0th percentile of their full history, and FedWatch implies 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63. Asia went the other way from the prior reading: the tracked A-share panel closed with all 11 names higher, led by 600584.SH at 7.7491 percent, after 10 of 11 had closed lower. The composite held at 46.47 with a day-over-day change of 0.0 and the regime remains goldilocks at a model confidence of 0.929, with the macro block at 64.94 the only binding constraint. Volatility is still not confirming, with VIX at 17.71 from 17.2 while equities advanced and the reverse repo facility at 0.276 scoring 96.47 on liquidity risk. In Europe overnight, political risk moved into sovereign spreads, with France's 10-year spread over Bund at 100 basis points, while the Bank of Japan's cautious post-hike guidance left the yen at 153.71 per dollar.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The discount rate has no cushion left and the repricing has moved to the front end: the 10-year sits at 5.01 and the 10-year real rate at 2.68, both at the 100.0th percentile of their full history, while the 2-year rose to 4.74 from 4.67.
Macro is the heaviest and still-rising block at 64.94, and policy is still priced as a hike: FedWatch implies 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63.
The liquidity cushion is thin: the reverse repo facility at 0.276 sits in the 1.77th percentile and carries a liquidity risk score of 96.47, even as reserves rose to 3013794.
Leadership is still narrow: semis relative sits at -16.3649 and small caps at -4.4557, so the equity bid is running through a smaller part of the market than the index level suggests.

Cross-asset confirmation is stuck at 0.5 and contributes 7.5 points, the single largest contribution, with only 5 of 10 internal signals triggered: the dollar at 118.2126, the real rate at 2.68, small-cap underperformance, gold and the high-yield/treasury spread are the flags that fired.

supporting_signals.claim: Equity structure improved for a second session: the share of names above their 200-day average rose to 0.5806 from 0.5677 and the new-highs ratio to 0.0387 from 0.0323.
Credit tightened alongside the equity bid for a second session: high-yield spreads at 2.70 from 2.76 and investment-grade at 0.78 from 0.80.

Sector breadth is broad rather than narrow: 20 of 22 tracked sectors and themes finished higher, led by memory at 4.8923, quantum computing at 4.8867 and semis leaders at 4.1739, with only digital advertising at -0.1212 and fintech at -0.0927 lower.
Crypto participated in the risk bid: BTC at 78195, ETH at 2515.33 and SOL at 106.39.

The tracked A-share panel closed with all 11 names higher, led by 600584.SH at 7.7491 percent and 300475.SZ at 6.2732 percent, the mirror image of the prior reading in which 10 of 11 had closed lower.

contradicting_signals.claim: Volatility refused to confirm the equity bid: VIX rose to 17.71 from 17.2 even as 20 of 22 sectors advanced, and the level sits only in the 50.24th percentile, so the signal is cheap rather than supportive.
Only 5 of 10 cross-asset signals fired, so the model keeps cross-asset confirmation at 0.5 and still treats the advance as unconfirmed by the full signal set.
Policy is still priced as a hike: FedWatch implies 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63, so an equity market rallying into a tightening path is fighting the policy signal.
European sovereign risk widened overnight: France's 10-year spread over Bund reached 100 basis points, and the EU economics commissioner warned that rising yields will be felt across Europe.

Realised vol at 9.6396 is the model's most benign reading, which is itself the problem: a complacent vol regime alongside a discount rate at the 100.0th percentile leaves the equity bid exposed to a vol repricing.

what_changed_today: The composite held at 46.47 with a day-over-day change of 0.0, keeping the caution state and the goldilocks regime.
The rate block repriced from the front end: the 2-year rose to 4.74 from 4.67 while the 10-year moved only to 5.01 from 5.00, leaving the 10Y/2Y curve at 0.27.
The 10-year real rate rose to 2.68 from 2.62 and the 5-year, 5-year forward breakeven to 2.34 from 2.31, so this is a real-rate repricing rather than an inflation-expectation one.
Equity structure improved a second day: 0.5806 of names sit above their 200-day average from 0.5677, and the new-highs ratio is 0.0387 from 0.0323.
The tracked A-share panel flipped to broad strength, closing with all 11 names higher, led by 600584.SH at 7.7491 percent, after 10 of 11 had closed lower in the prior reading.
Overnight European sovereign spreads widened, with France's 10-year spread over Bund at 100 basis points, and the EU economics commissioner put fiscal prudence first.
watch_next: Whether the front end keeps leading: with the 2-year at 4.74 and the 10-year at 5.01, a further short-end move would tighten a discount rate that already sits at the 100.0th percentile.
The FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 and the high-importance Personal Income and Outlays and GDP releases on 2026-09-30.
Whether credit keeps tightening against rising yields: high-yield at 2.70 and investment-grade at 0.78 sit at the low end of their range and have little further room.
Whether the reverse repo facility at 0.276 refills and reserves at 3013794 keep rising, which is the difference between a drained cushion and funding stress.

Whether the A-share panel confirms its advance with all 11 names higher in a second session, and whether European sovereign spreads stay contained around France's 10-year spread over Bund of 100 basis points.

bull_case.title: Bull: the front-end repricing is absorbed and breadth keeps improving
points: Credit keeps tightening from 2.70 and the 2-year stabilises at 4.74, so the bid that lifted 20 of 22 sectors extends.
Breadth carries: 0.5806 above the 200-day average and a new-highs ratio of 0.0387 leave room before the structure looks stretched.
Volatility gives way: a VIX print below 17.71, from the 50.24th percentile, removes the last cross-asset non-confirmation.

base_case.title: Base: the composite stays flat while leadership rotates inside the AI complex
points: The composite holds near 46.47 with the macro block at 64.94 as the binding constraint, so the headline stays at caution even as sectors rotate.
The goldilocks regime survives as long as breadth above the 200-day average holds near 0.5806 and realised vol stays at 9.6396.
Leadership stays inside AI: memory at 4.8923, quantum computing at 4.8867 and semis leaders at 4.1739 against digital advertising at -0.1212.

bear_case.title: Bear: the discount rate tightens from the short end and the narrow structure breaks
points: The front end extends: with the 10-year at 5.01 and the real rate at 2.68 both at the 100.0th percentile, a further move in the 2-year from 4.74 leaves valuations no cushion.
Liquidity amplifies it: the reverse repo facility at 0.276 sits in the 1.77th percentile, so a reserves draw shows up first in funding rather than in prices.
Volatility reprices: VIX at 17.71 in only the 50.24th percentile is cheap protection, and semis relative at -16.3649 shows how narrow leadership already is.
